source.title: Discrepancies are Virtue: Weak-to-Strong Generalization through Lens of Intrinsic Dimension
source.authors: Yijun Dong; Yi-Chen Li; Yunai Li; Jason D. Lee; Qi Lei

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains strong students on weak-model pseudo-labels and reports weak-to-strong performance, including PGR, across synthetic, vision and language settings. It uses the original W2S intervention and PGR measure, though its theoretical framework and some experimental procedures differ.
record.gate_note: The paper reports PGR and OPR results and comparisons of weak-to-strong, weak, strong supervised fine-tuning and strong-ceiling models. The SST-2 experiment uses Burns et al.'s confidence-weighted loss, but does not compare it with naive fine-tuning, so it does not test V2. Numerical values visible only in plots are recorded as figure only; cited results from other papers are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper gives a theory (ridgeless and ridge regression) of when a student trained on weak pseudo-labels beats its teacher. It checks this with its own W2S experiments reporting Burns et al.'s PGR: synthetic regression, UTKFace and ColoredMNIST linear probing, and SST-2 full fine-tuning. The method differs from the original suite (mostly linear probes on fixed features, a fixed student, a theoretical framing), so T2 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct; two findings should be added. The authors conclude that, in the variance-dominated regime, W2S comes from variance reduction in the teacher feature directions the student does not share. Lower overlap and a lower student intrinsic dimension (ds < dw) both help, and more label noise raises PGR. Absolute W2S error falls with more data, but PGR and OPR can fall as labeled n grows. The mechanism may differ when bias dominates.
record.recipe_differences: Uses weak-model pseudo-labels to fine-tune a stronger model and reports Burns et al.'s PGR. Vision experiments mostly use linear probing on pretrained features; the SST-2 experiment uses full fine-tuning and a confidence-weighted loss. The paper also develops a ridgeless/ridge regression theory rather than reproducing the original experimental suite.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome changes with feature-subspace overlap, intrinsic dimensions, labeled sample size n, pseudo-label sample size N, and injected label noise. The paper reports relative-performance degeneration as n grows in some settings and improvement as N or injected noise increases.

fits_no_version.finding: OPR: ratio of strong-SFT excess risk (student trained on the same n gold labels) to W2S excess risk. W2S beats the strong SFT baseline only at low overlap and moderate n, and loses as n grows (Figs 1, 2, 4, 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: W2S on N pseudo-labels beats direct supervised fine-tuning of the strong model on the teacher's n labels only when student–teacher feature overlap is low and n is moderate.

record.problems: Several empirical results are only plotted and lack numerical values in the text. UTKFace intrinsic dimensions and feature overlap are estimated from the full dataset, including test data, as stated by the authors. The theoretical results rely on specific regression, feature-distribution and sample-size assumptions; the paper notes limits to its bias analysis. Some vision and language task descriptions do not state uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant results omitted. The paper's plotted teacher-by-teacher curves are represented by the reported comparative trends; exact plotted points are not recoverable from the text and are marked figure only.

untested.parts: No auxiliary-loss, ensembling or loss-variant comparison against naive fine-tuning. SST-2 uses the confidence loss throughout.
No sweep of student size within a task (the student is fixed per task); no chess or reward-modelling tasks.
No distribution shift, no exploitation of unverifiable supervision, and no error-similarity measure. Feature-subspace overlap is related but is not error similarity.
Only UTKFace regression and ColoredMNIST classification, both by linear probing; no full-fine-tuning vision results.
Bias advantage not quantified (footnote 6); the bias-dominated regime is not analysed.

missing.what: Per-teacher UTKFace MSE curves: W2S vs weak, strong SFT and ceiling. W2S beats the weak teacher with enough n and N; at large n it may lose to strong SFT; ds < dw gives lower W2S MSE.
missing.locator: Appendix E.1, Figures 7–9 and bullet text

missing.what: Ridge-regression extension (Theorem 3): W2S variance bounded by cdN(Σw,Σs), so less similar features give lower risk; the leading inherited term is not removed by larger N.
W2S in bias: when ρs = 0 and ds < dw, the student has strictly lower bias than the teacher.
Measured intrinsic and correlation dimensions per teacher, needed to interpret the overlap trends.

record.verdict_notes: The study is mainly theoretical. Except SST-2, experiments are linear probes on fixed features with a single fixed student per task, so Burns' student-size trend is not tested. Many results are figure-only; states rest on plot axes and the text's trend statements. Intrinsic and correlation dimensions were estimated on the full dataset including test data. The SST-2 run uses the confidence-weighted loss without a naive baseline, so it says nothing on V2.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments are regression or classification tasks in the paper's stated settings; they do not establish the effect for all pretrained model families or tasks.
No comparison of auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling, or loss variants against naive fine-tuning.
The study varies weak-teacher models and feature-subspace overlap, and studies multiple tasks. It does not sweep strong-student size within a task or test reward modelling.
No distribution-shift test or test of gains shrinking because weak and strong models make similar errors. Feature-subspace overlap is studied, which is not the same as error similarity.
The theory concerns ridgeless or ridge regression under stated feature, noise and dimensionality assumptions; it does not establish an unconditional guarantee for arbitrary models or tasks.
Vision is tested on UTKFace age regression and ColoredMNIST classification; other non-language modalities are not tested.

rows.subject: fw2s (theoretical strong student)
rows.size_stated: intrinsic dimension ds; ds, dw ≪ d
rows.stage_stated: ridgeless regression fine-tuning on weak pseudo-labels
rows.operation_detail: Fit the strong features to pseudo-labels from a weak model trained on n noisy labels, using N pseudo-labels.

conditions.value: jointly Gaussian; low-rank feature subspaces; n > dw + 1
n = dw + q + 1, with q ≥ max{1, ds − dw + 1} for the PGR lower bound

rows.baseline: Weak-teacher to strong-ceiling excess-risk gap, as defined in the paper
rows.value: PGR ≥ 1 − dw2s(N)/dw − qρs/(dwσ²) − (q + dw)ρw/(dwσ²), where dw2s(N) = ds∧w + (dw − ds∧w)ds/N
rows.note: The bound supports positive gap recovery under suitable small-error and low-overlap/sample-size conditions; it is a conditional lower bound, not a universal positive-PGR result.
rows.check: This is a theoretical bound, not an empirical W2S result, so it bears on V5 only. Within its stated assumptions it gives the condition for PGR > 0, so 'partial' understates it; the conditions are scope, not weakness.

rows.subject: fw2s (theoretical strong student)
rows.size_stated: intrinsic dimension ds; ds, dw ≪ d
rows.stage_stated: ridgeless regression fine-tuning on weak pseudo-labels
rows.operation_detail: Characterize the strong student's variance and bias under the stated regression model.

conditions.value: jointly Gaussian for exact variance; low-rank feature subspaces

rows.value: Var(fw2s) = [σ²/(n − dw − 1)](ds∧w + (dw − ds∧w)ds/N); Bias(fw2s) ≤ Bias(fw) + ρs
rows.note: The analysis says variance is inherited on the overlapping subspace and reduced on the discrepancy subspace; thus improvement depends on sample size and feature overlap.
rows.check: Exact variance characterization: Var(fw2s) < Var(fw) whenever N > ds and ds∧w < dw. Within the assumptions this is the claimed condition, not a partial one.
